text:
sophia: quick note — ran a long-tail soak with AWQ quant + fp8 KV cache casting on 40B and hit OOMs when batch_size=8 around token 340. reproducible locally and on dedicated node.
omar: ouch. which allocator config were you on? slab or buddy?
sophia: slabpool, default slab_size=64MB, workspace_limit=1GB. logs show a lot of tiny allocations during kernel fallback which never get reclaimed.
chris: can you paste the small profiler snippet? curious if it's kernel selection + casting blowup or just kv dtype doubling.
sophia: profiler excerpt: 
```
PROFILE STEP 1: kern=attention_opt_fast, time=1.9ms, peak_mem=18.2MB
PROFILE STEP 2: kern=matmul_fp8_fallback, time=4.2ms, peak_mem=72.6MB
PROFILE KV: cache_read_cast(fp32->fp8) time=0.9ms, extra_mem=40.0MB
GC HINT: slab_free candidates=24, tiny_allocs=136
```
omar: that matmul fallback + cast looks like the culprit. matmul_fp8_fallback allocates full-size temp buffers in fp32 during transpose, then casts, so we get both footprints.
mike: we've seen similar with mixed-precision transposes — kernel does allocate a scratch FP32 workspace then quantizes to AWQ layout. If workspace_limit is tight, allocator fragments and triggers OOM instead of reclaiming tiny regions.
chris: two orthogonal mitigations: 1) prefer a kernel path that streams cast in-place or does out-of-core chunked transpose; 2) tweak allocator to proactively coalesce tiny free regions and maintain a mini-cache for small buffers used by fallback kernels.
omar: i can prototype a "reclaim-on-fallback" hook that does a quick sweep of slab freelist if a fallback kernel requests >X bytes. should be low-risk.
sophia: that'd help. also think about KV cache dtype policy: for AWQ we currently keep KV in fp32 then cast at read-time. switching to store in fp16 for short-context may halve kv footprint. tradeoff is precision for long-context.
mike: agree. we should add a per-model kv_storage_dtype config (auto policy): - if model quantized AWQ/GPTQ and seq_len<1024 -> prefer fp16; else keep fp32.
chris: small config prototype (pseudocode):
```
kv_policy = {
  "auto": True,
  "threshold_seq_len": 1024,
  "fp16_for_awq": True
}
```
omar: on allocator side i'll try two patches: (A) mini-pool reclaim sweep on kernel fallback, (B) compact-scan that merges adjacent free slabs when fragmentation>20%. will run perf harness.
sophia: thanks. can we also add a quick perf test case: AWQ-40B, batch=8, seq=384 and collect peak_rss, fragmentation ratio, fallback_count. we need numbers before/after.
mike: will add harness to eng-runtime/perf with those metrics and a small dashboard. tagging @infra-bot to reserve a 40B dedicated slot tonight.
infra-bot: reserved node rwd-dedicated-40b-03 for 2h starting 2026-03-18T02:00:00Z :white_check_mark:
chris: one more note — consider adding an in-kernel flag to prefer low-memory matmul kernels when batch*seq exceeds threshold. kernel selection policy currently only optimizes latency; add memory-aware scoring.
sophia: exactly. memory-aware kernel selection + proactive reclaim should fix the regression without harming perf for smaller cases.
omar: i'll push a branch with reclaim-first and a test that intentionally triggers fallback and asserts no OOM. will ping when ready.
mike: cool. action list: 1) omar: reclaim & compaction patch; 2) chris: memory-aware kernel selector heuristic; 3) sophia: perf runs + KV dtype policy results; 4) mike: dashboard + slot. target: run nightly and report tomorrow.
sophia: thanks all — i'll attach the full logs and the AWQ config in the issue. :thumbsup:
